title: Longest substring without repeats
prompt: Implement lengthOfLongestSubstring(s string) int: the length of the longest substring with no repeated character. One pass, O(n).
explanation: The window is valid when it holds no duplicate. Jumping left to j+1 (never backwards, hence the j >= left guard) is what keeps it O(n): "dvdf" is the case that catches a left pointer that moves back.
hints: Window [left, right]; the map remembers where each byte was last seen.
On a repeat, left only ever moves forward: left = max(left, lastSeen+1).
refs: LC 3 Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters

title: Balanced brackets
prompt: Implement isValid(s string) bool for a string of ()[]{}: brackets must close in the right order.
explanation: Two failure modes, and both need a check: a closer with the wrong (or no) top, and leftovers on the stack at the end. Dropping the second one makes "(" pass.
hints: Push openers, and on a closer check the top of the stack.
Two ways to return false: a closer with an empty or mismatched stack, and a non-empty stack at the end.

title: Reverse a linked list
prompt: Implement reverseList(head *ListNode) *ListNode in place, iteratively. ListNode, buildList and listVals are already defined for you.
explanation: Three pointers, and the order is the whole drill: save next before you clobber cur.Next, then walk prev and cur forward. You return prev, not cur, because the loop exits with cur == nil.
hints: Three pointers: prev, cur, and the next you must save before overwriting.
Save next, point cur at prev, then slide prev and cur forward. Return prev.

title: Validate a BST with bounds
prompt: Implement isValidBST(root *TreeNode) bool. Every node in the left subtree must be strictly less than the node, every node on the right strictly greater, all the way down. TreeNode is already defined.
explanation: Comparing each node only with its two children is the classic wrong answer: it accepts a 4 buried in the right subtree of 5. Correctness needs an inherited (lo, hi) range that narrows on the way down.
hints: Checking each node against its two children is not enough; a deep descendant can still violate.
Pass a (low, high) bound down; going left tightens high, going right tightens low.

title: House robber in O(1) space
prompt: Implement rob(nums []int) int: the maximum sum of a subset of nums with no two adjacent elements. Use two rolling variables, not a table.
explanation: cur is the best over houses 0..i, prev the best over 0..i-1. Each house is max(skip = cur, take = prev+v). [2,1,1,2] is the case that catches a greedy "alternate houses" solution.
hints: At each house the choice is take it plus what you had two back, or skip it and keep the best so far.
Two rolling ints: prev2 and prev1, updated as cur = max(prev1, prev2+n).

title: Merge overlapping intervals
prompt: Implement merge(intervals [][]int) [][]int, each interval a [start, end] pair, returning the merged set sorted by start. Touching intervals like [1,4] and [4,5] merge. A sortByStart(intervals) helper is already defined for you.
explanation: Sorting by start is what makes a single pass enough: any interval that overlaps the running one must start inside it. The two traps are [1,4],[2,3] (the new end can be smaller, so take the max) and forgetting that <= merges touching intervals.
hints: Sort by start first, then walk once holding the interval you are currently extending.
Overlap means next.start <= cur.end; then cur.end = max(cur.end, next.end).

title: Count subarrays summing to k
prompt: Implement subarraySum(nums []int, k int) int: how many contiguous subarrays sum to exactly k. Values may be negative, so a sliding window will not work. O(n).
explanation: sum(i..j) == prefix[j] - prefix[i-1], so each running sum asks how many earlier prefixes equal sum-k. The seed counts[0] = 1 is the empty prefix, and without it every subarray starting at index 0 is missed.
hints: A subarray sum is a difference of two prefix sums.
Count prefix sums in a map, seeded with sum 0 -> 1, and at each step add counts[sum-k].
